text.p: Dollar/mark, after vaulting above the 1.88 level for the first time in nearly eight years, is now targeting an objective at 1.8875/80 in a bull channel from July 10, analysts said on Tuesday.

However, chart levels may not offer much resistance at lofty levels with a dollar/mark rally running essentially on momentum and showing no sign of top in the absence of German resolve to defend its currency, they added.
"The upside target is 1.8880, the projection in a bull channel from July 10," said senior analyst Scott Siller at MCM CurrencyWatch.
Other analysts' projections set at 1.8775 marks the target for the bull channel from the July 10 low of 1.7456.
Dollar/mark soared on Tuesday to 1.8832, its high from October 1989 when it peaked at 1.9921. In another bullish sign, the pullback from the high was limited to 1/2 pfennig only, they noted.

"If we take out the 1.8880-mark objective, you steepen the slope of the trend and then, the sky's the limit on that one," predicted Siller who put the next target at 1.92 "and then above 2.0450 or so."
The dollar/mark high in 1989 was set in June at 2.0478.
"Dollar/mark is rallying on pure momentum. It took out massive levels and that was sustained," agreed senior currency strategist Chris Turner at I.D.E.A.
"There is no sign, really, that a top is in place for the dollar, no real technical levels left. There are people talking about 2.05 marks," Turner added.
Dollar/mark should draw further help from the mark's all-around weakness, analysts predicted.
Sterling/mark took out 3.0445, the 62-percent retracement of the July slide from 3.0885 to 2.9725. Mark/yen faltered anew and is seen revisiting its recent 63.92 low.
Dollar/French franc also rose to its highest since October 1989 at 6.3560, with the next big level above 6.50.
Dollar/yen was a winner too, climbing to 119.38 and holding well above support at 119, the 50-percent retracement of the 1997 high/low move.

The next big level is at 119.95, the objective in daily studies that have turned increasingly bullish. Meanwhile, 120 is likely to offer strong psychological resistance amid market fears the Bank of Japan will not allow further deterioration. Past this, 121 is the objective as the 62-percent retracement of the 1997 high/low move. (( Isabelle Clary, 212-859-1666))
